column5: why
Detects logon and credential abuse (4624/4625) — the base for D4, D10
Kerberos TGT activity — base for D3 (AS-REP roasting)
Service ticket requests — base for D2 (Kerberoasting, RC4 4769)
Group membership changes — base for D1 (privileged group add)
Account create/enable/delete — base for joiner/leaver anomalies
Rogue computer accounts
Replication rights (4662) — base for D11 (DCSync)
Object changes in AD — supports the P10 change log
Interactive logons (4624) — base for D10 (Tier 0 / break-glass)
Session end — completes the timeline
Lockout bursts — supports D4 (spraying) investigation
Elevated/administrative logons — base for D10
Disconnects, reconnects, RDP — helps build the session timeline
Process start events; requires the command-line policy below to be useful
Process end; pairs with creation for a clean timeline
Someone turning auditing off is itself an event (defence evasion)
Domain policy changes
Privilege assignment changes
Debug/backup privileges — often used to read protected files
Share access at a coarse level
Sensitive-share access failures only (high volume — enabled on FS01 alone)
Allowed network connections; supports lateral-movement analysis
Driver and system integrity events
Backup and restore activity
